title: Latiq ErrorEnvelope
description: The one error shape every Latiq surface returns. An actionable: `kind` to branch on, `audience` for who can fix it, `retryable` for whether to send the call again, `facts` for the values behind `message`, `suggest` for the next call, `see` for the resource that explains the kind, and `trace_id` for the request that failed.

kind.description: The closed taxonomy of what went wrong. Classified by the failure, never by which call raised it.

message.description: One sentence on what went wrong, rendered from `facts` wherever it quotes a number or a name. Never empty: an error with nothing to read is not an actionable.

location.description: Where in the caller's SQL the error was found, so a client can point at it rather than restating the whole statement.

suggest.description: The NEXT CALL to make, copy-paste ready. There is deliberately no separate `next` field; this is it.

see.description: A `latiq://` resource URI about this kind — the deeper learning path. Must resolve to a resource the MCP surface actually serves.

audience.description: Who can actually fix this. `agent`: the caller, from a call it can make. `operator`: whoever runs the deployment. Two-valued on purpose — a variant no envelope can carry is a dead variant.

retryable.description: Whether to send this call again. `never`: not this call, ever. `as_is`: the same call, unchanged. `after_change`: the same call with corrected arguments.

facts.description: The named values behind `message` — measured numbers and given names, so a client branches on a value instead of parsing prose. Scalars only, by design: a string, a non-negative integer, or a boolean.

trace_id.description: The W3C trace id (32 lowercase hex digits) of the request that failed, so a caller can cite the id of its own failed request.
